phase_name: Fixture -- reproduce the batch shape and prove the bleed is gone

objectives.description: Build the fixture scaffold: throwaway git repo, real dispatch-worktree.sh/git-commit-scoped.sh/task-lock.sh/lake-build-guard.sh, no network, no real Lean toolchain

Case 1-2: two worktree-isolated candidates edit the same line of a shared markdown file distinctly; assert no bleed on the clean land and an honest conflict verdict (branch/worktree preserved) on the second
Case 3: mode-2 leg -- separate .lake directories per worktree via a stubbed lake (LAKE_BUILD_GUARD_LAKE_BIN), one unguarded call and one guarded call, assert no cross-worktree marker collision
Case 4: shared-tree counterpart -- hand-built contention manifest, first committer succeeds, second (with a manually-held claim simulating a live rival) refused with nothing staged
Case 5: negative control -- same edit pattern on a shared tree WITHOUT --task silently bleeds, proving Case 1's no-bleed assertion is not vacuous
Case 6: full teardown assertions across every repo (worktrees, branches, registry, claims, manifest all empty)

Debug pass: fixed a lake-build-guard.sh missing-lakefile refusal, a --dir-vs-cwd misunderstanding (the wrapped lake always runs from the guard's own CWD, not --dir), and two commit-count/branch-cleanup fixture bugs
Register the new test file in agent-system/extensions/core/manifest.json (provides.scripts) so deploy-headless.sh does not silently omit it
Verify: 41/41 assertions passing, shellcheck clean, check-task-references.sh clean (task-ref-ok:begin/:end wrapping every synthetic task-shaped fixture literal)

approaches_tried.approach: Pass --dir <worktree-path> to lake-build-guard.sh from the main tree's own CWD
approaches_tried.reason: --dir only steers project-root resolution for the lock/result file paths; the wrapped lake command itself always runs from the guard's own current process CWD (main.sh never cd's into ROOT before cmd_build). The build marker landed in the main tree's .lake/, not the worktree's. Fixed by cd-ing into the worktree itself before invoking the guard, with no --dir flag.

deviations.description: Run the real dispatch-prep path (orchestrate-cycle-plan.sh's own selection/provisioning) so each candidate is selected for isolation and provisioned
deviations.reason: Interpreted as driving the REAL dispatch-worktree.sh provision/land/release and git-commit-scoped.sh --task refusal directly (the actual lifecycle machinery Phases 4-9 built), rather than additionally re-driving orchestrate-cycle-plan.sh's OWN selection/manifest-producer code paths -- those are already covered end to end by Groups 30-31 in test-orchestrate-cycle-plan.sh. This fixture's job is the cross-script INTEGRATION outcome (no bleed, honest conflict, separate .lake/, refused shared-tree commit, clean teardown), matching the plan's own Verification bullets for this phase.

deviations.description: Verify the no-bleed assertion is not vacuous by temporarily forcing orchestrate-cycle-plan.sh's task_selected_for_worktree_isolation() predicate false
deviations.reason: That predicate lives in a different script this fixture does not otherwise drive (see the 10.2 deviation above). Case 5 substitutes a comparative negative control instead: the IDENTICAL two-writer same-file edit pattern run on a shared tree with the V5 refusal omitted (no --task), which DOES silently bleed -- proving Case 1's no-bleed assertion is not vacuous by directly reproducing the failure the posture closes, which is a stronger and more literal proof than toggling an internal predicate flag would have been.

deviations.description: Assert full teardown: no leftover worktrees, branches, locks, claims, or manifests
deviations.reason: dispatch-worktree.sh's own `release` deliberately never deletes a branch (durable git history, left for inspection -- see that script's own header). A teardown assertion expecting zero orchestrate/task-* branches therefore cannot rely on `release` alone; the fixture explicitly deletes each candidate's branch itself after landing/resolving it, the same way an operator would, then asserts the fully clean end state.
